coverage_note: Long English-only stretches: 07:00-08:15 (raa7/rawwa7 discussion), 21:18-23:53 (fi ishi enkasar word order), 1:03:26-1:05:02 (Farsi chat). Not rows: 06:46 'rah ... metakhri' -> Amal روّح, but she said راح is also fine ('Yeah عادي... the better word') - both-valid, skipped. 44:12 شهرها/شهرك for شعرك (Amal 'شهر is month') = dropped ع, S4 pronunciation; he self-fixed the -ha ending to -ak. 39:52 الآن for ألوان (Amal 'very close') and 27:52 كسا for كسر read as sound slips (S4). 26:47 عطلوا -> أتلوا self-fix of قاتلوا after her model. 38:27 بواتك -> كندرتك: she had asked for formal shoes, chat lists both, not an error. 08:27 asawi is on her sheet (do / make | Sawwi). 02:37 'قمت إمني ووشربت' unclear (maybe نمت منيح). 58:00 'maqtarakhar' unclear Latin. 1:00:29 تذكرتني accepted, Amal offered itzakaratni as an alternative. Echo candidates: 06:59 'Bara.' = his own Latin barra (away), not an echo; 'Two sec.', 'Neh.', 'Why' are English. laazem_noun 31:30 filed as B2 (Amal gave present نغير).

rows.medi_said: بدأت شغلي على تـ- تسعة ونص.
rows.why: Clock time takes el-saa3a (or el-): 'at nine thirty' is 3ala el-saa3a tis3a w nus; Amal reacted only to him answering 'when' instead of 'where'.
rows.english: I started my work at nine thirty.

rows.medi_said: معروف is ground؟ معروف؟ No. ... What was What was ground؟
rows.why: He asked for the word for 'ground' (beef) after trying معروف / مرفوف; Amal supplied مفروم (sheet: ground beef | La7meh mafrumeh).
خضرا (vegetables, non-human plural) takes a feminine adjective; he wavered to مختلفه and settled on masculine مختلف, Amal let it pass (my reading).

rows.amal_said: Yeah, we don't say that yesterday. Just yesterday is its own...
rows.why: امبارح never takes el-; Amal had modeled نفس مبارح at 05:27 and then explained the rule; his 05:37 نفس امبارح repeated her model.
Telling what his cousin did yesterday needs past أجا; Amal recast and he repeated أجا.
He said 'came from my house' meaning 'came to my house'; Amal said no, أجا على (later أجا عندي), and he repeated أجا على بيتي.

rows.medi_said: So I know bafadal. Is it one of my words?
rows.why: He did not recognise her بتفضل (thought it was 'fatad / choose') and asked; Amal explained بفضل = I prefer (sheet: i prefer | Ana bafaddel). Didn't-know on listening.
Amal asked حبيت (did you like) how we practised; he answered with حكيتلي (you told me), mishearing her word; she repeated حبيت.
Defining بكسر as 'I make something broken' needs the habitual present بخلّي; he used bare خلّي and Amal let it pass.

rows.chat: e7na benfaddel enno inti ma tekserih
rows.why: After 'we prefer (that) you...' the second verb drops b-; Amal recast ما تكسري and her chat shows ma tekserih, he then said ما تكسريه.
rows.english: we prefer you don't break it

rows.why: 'I broke it' needs the object ending -o on the verb; Amal recast كسرته and he repeated it.
'What broke them' needs the doing verb كسر, not the happening verb انكسر (which cannot take an object); Amal recast and he said 'It's inflicting'.

rows.amal_said: تكسري. What's plural of أشي إشي؟ ... تكسري أشياء.
rows.why: 'things' is plural; Amal asked for the plural of إشي and supplied أشياء.
rows.english: since when do you break things?

rows.why: سنين means years; teeth is سنان. Amal recast and asked what سنين is, he answered 'year' and fixed to سنانها.
He had just been told the plural كاسات and produced كسرات; Amal recast Kasat and he said 'كاسات, that's right' (sheet: cup | Kaasa).

rows.medi_said: Uh, قتلو مع بعض ... Is it مع بعض or بعض؟
rows.why: 'Fought each other' is قاتلوا بعض with no مع (مع بعض = together); Amal had modeled قتلوا بعض at 27:12 and answered in English 'each other', he then said 'Not fought together'.

rows.chat: el-walaad 2aatalu ba3ad u wa7ad minhom kasar
rows.why: 'One of the boys' needs من; Amal prompted with 'واحد of the children' and he added من, she then offered منهم.

rows.amal_said: or of them. One of them.
rows.why: After من the known boys keep el- (من الولاد); Amal steered him to منهم instead of fixing it, and later confirmed واحد من الولاد works.
'I change MY mind' needs the possessive ending رأيي; Amal recast and he repeated (sheet: i change my mind | Ba8ayyer ra2yi).

rows.medi_said: We should... Okay. احنا كان لازم--
rows.amal_said: we just should. we not should have.
rows.why: كان لازم means 'should have'; Amal said it is just 'should', not 'should have'.

rows.medi_said: اه. احنا لازم، غيّرنا ... Yeah, بنغير.
rows.why: After لازم the verb is a bare present; he used past غيّرنا, then بنغير with b-; Amal said 'present', then recast نغير.

rows.medi_said: The time of the flight. وقت ال... اه... flight. Oh my God.
rows.why: He could not find 'flight/plane' and said it in English; Amal cued 'remember car' (سيارة) and he produced طيارة (sheet: airplane / flight | 6ayyaara).

rows.amal_said: very close. بس السيارة، السيارة feminine or masculine؟ غيرت.
rows.why: طيارة is feminine so the verb is تغيرت; Amal asked feminine or masculine and he fixed it.

rows.medi_said: امتى برنامجك... تغيرت؟ Program shift feminine.
rows.why: برنامج is masculine so the verb is تغير; Amal said program is masculine and he fixed to تغير.
After لازم the verb is a bare present يتغيروا, not past اتغيروا; Amal recast and he said 'is that past tense?... It's present tense'.

rows.amal_said: تغير أو تغيري حالك أو حالك. Make it consistent. Make the gender consistent.
rows.why: Masculine verb تغير with feminine حالك; Amal named the gender-consistency rule and he said ما تغيري حالك (he thinks he said تغيري, she heard تغير).
The first word of an idafa takes no el-: يوم الاجتماع; he started اليوم, Amal prompted 'day of the meeting' and he said يوم الاجتماع.
rows.english: why did the meeting day change?

rows.amal_said: It did change. Why did it change? It did change.
rows.why: 'Why did it change' is past تغير; he used present بتغيّر, Amal repeated 'did change' and he said 'past tense... تغير'.

rows.amal_said: Again. Photograph me. You photograph me.
rows.why: The command 'photograph me' is صوريني (doing form, command shape); he used تصوريني, Amal said 'again' and he fixed to صوريني.

rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. That's the error I was talking about. So cam takes singular.
rows.why: After كم the noun is singular; Amal named the rule and he said كم صورة.
'Do you get photographed' is the t- (get) form بتتصوري; Amal contrasted the two and he said 'that's right, بتتصوري'.
rows.english: do you get photographed a lot?

rows.why: A plain present verb takes b- (بيعرف, as in her chat and her 54:15 بيعرف يصور); she offered it as an alternative, not a fix.
After يعرف the second verb drops b-; the engine wrote بيصوّر and Medi thought he said b-, but Amal says she heard يصور, so no voiced fix.

rows.amal_said: First do the left, left past. Make it past.
rows.why: 'When I traveled the world' needs past لفيت; Amal said 'make it past' and he said لما لفيت.
rows.english: when I went around the world

rows.amal_said: I bring. ... To bring, but who's bringing? You are bringing.
rows.why: 'Remind me to bring': the speaker brings, so أجيب; Amal asked who is bringing and he fixed to أجيب.
'I reminded him' needs the him-ending -o; he said -ak (you) then -no, Amal recast Zakarto and he repeated زكرته.
'They didn't remember me' needs ما before the verb; Amal said 'Didn't' and he added ما.
'He doesn't remember' is habitual present ما بيتذكر; he used past, Amal recast and he said 'it's present tense'.
Amal recast his plural أسامي as أسماء (her chat el-asmaa2).

rows.medi_said: Uh, أسامي, um? ... I don't know.
rows.amal_said: As it's general, so what do we add? ... Il asma.
rows.why: Names in general take el-; Amal asked what we add, he did not know, she supplied Il asma and he repeated el asma.

rows.amal_said: الكل؟ ... كل الكلمات؟ ... كل شي. You could say كل شي.
rows.why: الكل means everyone; for 'everything / all the words' Amal questioned الكل and gave كل شي / كل الكلمات, he said كل شي.
rows.english: I want to practise everything a lot
